title: Quarter velocity claims and manager prep (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose: quick, conversational scripts + three concise impact claims that I can use in a 1:1 or calibration. This is a working scratchpad — short phrases I can memorize and evidence snippets to back them up.

Structure:
- 3 claims (one-liners)
- Proof bullets (metric or concrete example, 1–2 lines)
- 90-day plan / ask (what I want, why it moves the needle, success signal)
- Calibration cues + potential objections and short responses
- Notes to self / follow-ups

CLAIM 1: I accelerated offer-to-first-day time by streamlining onboarding content and automations.
Proof:
- Reduced average new hire activation time from ~6 days to ~2.4 days for ICs in Q4 by removing a manual provisioning step and adding a templated welcome doc (measured across 18 hires).
- Example: engineering cohort onboarded 4 hires in one week with zero provisioning tickets; hiring manager feedback: "hired -> productive faster" (Noah notes).
Why it matters: faster ramp increases first-quarter productivity and reduces lost days; visible to hiring managers and finance.

CLAIM 2: I built a lightweight experiment to improve manager calibration and it produced a measurable change in calibration behavior.
Proof:
- Ran a 6-week micro-experiment (pilot with 8 managers): a 10-min pre-calibration checklist + two short prompts in 1:1 templates. 75% of managers reported changing at least one promotion eligibility note; 3 promotion packets were improved before submission.
- Linked artifact: pilot checklist + sample 1:1 script (CONFLUENCE-people-ops-quarterly-reads).
Why it matters: higher-quality packets reduce review friction and repeated asks during calibration cycles.

CLAIM 3: I reduced cross-team time-to-resolution for HR operational tickets by creating a triage matrix and a micro-runbook.
Proof: 
- Median ticket TTL dropped from ~48 hours to ~18 hours for Level-1/2 ops issues over the quarter (tracking in JIRA-HR-452).
- Runbook decreased handoffs (SRE & infra) by clarifying ownership: 40% fewer escalations to platform engineering.
Why it matters: reliability for people operations increases trust and reduces churn risk.

90-DAY PLAN / ASK (concise):
- Request: +0.4 FTE (contracted) to own onboarding automations and backlog grooming for 3 months.
- Why: current backlog growth (+25% month-over-month) is delaying planned improvements; dedicated time will enable another iteration of automation and a second experiment for manager calibration at scale.
- Success signals: onboarding activation time consistently <3 days across cohorts; calibration checklist adoption >=60% among target managers; backlog reduction by 40%.

Calibration cues / likely questions + short scripts:
- "How do you know that onboarding change caused the drop in activation time?"
  Script: We A/B'd content delivery timing (old manual step vs. templated welcome + auto-provision) across two small cohorts and tracked activation; correlation held after controlling for role. Noah reviewer notes attached.
- "Is the calibration pilot scalable?"
  Script: Pilot uses a 2-step manager nudge and a reusable template. Scaling requires a mix of manager training and tooling — ask is for time to automate nudge insertion and measure adoption.
- "Why hire vs. contractor?"
  Script: Contractor reduces time to execute and lets us validate ROI before committing to headcount. If signals hit, propose conversion in Q3.

Risks / mitigations:
- Risk: Contractor doesn't ramp quickly -> Mitigation: 2-week onboarding checklist + shadowing plan; pair with Priya for first month.
- Risk: Metrics noise from hiring season -> Mitigation: use role-normalized activation time (percentile by role) and run A/A checks.

Quick 1:1 opening scripts (30–90 seconds):
- 30s: "Quick update: last quarter I focused on onboarding friction, manager calibration, and ops runbooks. The headline: activation time down ~60%, pilot shows calibration lift, and tickets are resolving faster. My ask is a short-term contractor to lock in the improvements and scale the calibration pilot — success metrics are activation <3 days and checklist adoption >=60%."
- 90s (if they ask for evidence): one-line metric, one short example, and the ask. "Activation time from 6 to 2.4 days — example: Eng cohort avoided provisioning delays. Pilot: 8 managers, changed behavior in 75% of them leading to 3 cleaner promotion packets. Contractor lets us automate the remaining manual steps."

Evidence bank (snippets to paste into messages):
- "Activation time reduced from ~6d to ~2.4d (n=18 hires, role-normalized) after removing manual provisioning step and adding templated welcome docs."
- "Calibration pilot (8 managers, 6 weeks) — 75% reported at least one change in packet quality; three packets improved prior to review."
- "Median ops TTL down from ~48h to ~18h (JIRA-HR-452); 40% fewer escalations to infra/SRE due to clarified ownership matrix."

Open questions / TODOs to self:
- Pull cohort-level activation time by role for the last 6 months to show trend (ask analytics for role-normalized view).
- Draft a one-pager for the contractor role + 6-week milestones.
- Confirm with finance on temporary contractor budget runway and conversion signal.
- Run A/A check on activation measurement method to be confident the signal is real.

Notes to self / style cues:
- Keep claims crisp: one sentence + one data point + one example.
- Anticipate calibration: give one concrete counterfactual (what would have happened without the change).
- Use manager scripts that start with a headline then the ask (people prefer concise top-of-message).
- Save a 2-line Slack DM variant for follow-up after 1:1: headline + link to evidence doc.

Revision log (scratch):
- 2025-11-18: created initial claims and rough metrics from JIRA and onboarding logs.
- 2025-12-09: added pilot feedback notes from Priya.
- 2026-03-05: updated activation numbers and added contractor ask; cleaned scripts.

Short-term micro-actions (this week):

- Draft contractor JD and send to Noah (tomorrow).
- Post 1:1 script in the people-ops shared channel for quick feedback (Friday).
